_meta.purpose: Mirror of the production schedule run rows AS RECORDED, so a suspicious computed number can be traced to its source lines without opening the workbook.
_meta.sheet_rows_unmatched_note: A handful of rows carry no sheet row number: the run key includes the start time, so a line edited in the workbook since the last overnight ingest no longer matches the stored row. It corrects itself on the next refresh.
_meta.sheet_row_note: 'Sheet row' is the row number on that workbook tab, so any published figure can be looked up and checked against the source. 'Actual time (as written)' is now the sheet's own text (0.15 = 15 minutes), NOT the decimal hours used for costing -- see 'Actual hrs (resolved)' for that.
_meta.no_actual_time_note: Split three ways by WHY the time is missing: start_equals_end (the sheet's own formula works out to 0.00), time_cell_not_a_time (a '.' where a clock time belongs), and no_actual_time (genuinely blank).
_meta.task_note: A row whose Item # is a task code (washing, cleaning, changeover, labor note, material handling) produces nothing BY DESIGN and is never flagged for having no output. The list lives in skills/_lib/taskcodes.py with its evidence; an unrecognised code defaults to PRODUCT so a real SKU cannot be silently dropped.
_meta.grace_note: A run sheet that has not been filled in yet is not a defect. Within 10 days the row reads 'sheet not filled in yet' and its missing-actual-time flag is withdrawn; past the window it stands.
_meta.future_note: The workbook is scheduled ~3 weeks ahead, so a date in the next 90 days means the job has not run yet -- it has made nothing because it has not happened. Beyond 90 days it is a date typo and keeps its mis-dated flag.
_meta.open_note: A row dated today, or with a start time and no end time, is still running -- its output is not knowable yet, so it is never flagged for having none. Not a defect: see the paperwork grace rule.
_meta.wo_group_key: (work order, item, station); '0' and blank treated as no work order
_meta.wo_note: A work order routinely takes MORE THAN ONE LINE (a break, or it finishes the next day). PLANNED qty is repeated on every line while ACTUAL qty and hours are split. Checks comparing output against a plan or a per-unit norm are evaluated on the WHOLE work order, not the line. Row-level checks (over-16h run, downtime vs runtime, missing crew size, missing standard) stay per line, because they describe one sitting at the machine.
_meta.suspect_note: Rows are FLAGGED, never dropped. Ingest flags (no_actual_time, misdate) are structural; the rest are arithmetic checks for rows that explode a computed cost or efficiency figure. Extremes are judged against the item's OWN median, not a global threshold. A flag is a prompt to look at the workbook line, not a verdict.
_meta.transform_note: Values are raw except 'Actual hrs (resolved)', which applies the adopted hh.mm time basis (10.33 = 10h33m) via costlib.resolve_actual_hours -- Start/End elapsed where available, hh.mm conversion as fallback. 'Actual time (as written)' is the untouched workbook value. No costing here.
_meta.uom_warning: 'Bad units' are FINISHED units; 'Bad component' are individual tea bags/envelopes. Different UOM -- never add them together.

columns.label: Workbook
columns.basis: Which workbook file the row was read from.

columns.label: Sheet row
columns.basis: The row number on that workbook tab. Read from the file itself.

columns.label: Station
columns.basis: The tab name mapped to the physical station it means (Production and AMS are the same line).

columns.label: WO line
columns.basis: Worked out here: which line this is of a work order that spans several rows, matched on work order + item + station.

columns.label: Actual hrs (resolved)
columns.basis: WORKED OUT, not off the sheet. The sheet writes time as hours.minutes (0.15 = 15 minutes); this is the same span in decimal hours, which is what cost is calculated from. The next column says which way round it was read.

columns.label: Time from
columns.basis: Which method gave the resolved hours: start_end = the clock times; hhmm_convert = the hours.minutes text; already_decimal = it was decimal to begin with.

columns.label: Row is
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from the Item # against a reviewed list of task codes (washing, cleaning, changeover, labor notes). Anything not on that list is treated as a product.

columns.label: Job state
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from the date and times: finished, still running (dated today or no end time), not run yet (dated ahead), or sheet not filled in yet (inside 10 days).

columns.label: Pack method
columns.basis: AN ESTIMATE, and the weakest column here. Nothing on the run sheet records which one was used. It reads 'boxpacker' purely because the row is on a pack station and its date falls on or after 2026-04-01, the date we believe the box packer came into use -- and that date is itself an estimate, taken from units per operator-hour stepping up in April plus a few Comments mentions of 'amy'. A note saying 'handpack' in Comments overrides it. Treat as an indication, never as a record of what happened.

columns.label: Flags
columns.basis: WORKED OUT by the checks described under 'What the flags mean'. Not a workbook field.
